prompt:
You are a blind code reader in an empirical software-engineering study. Work only from the files in the current directory.

1. Read protocol.md first.
2. Read batch.md. It names 20 Java files by id, their path in their repository, and their local copy under files/.
3. For every file: read the whole file (use Read with offset and limit for files over 2000 lines, do not skip the tail). Identify the method with the highest cognitive complexity (the one with the most and deepest nested branches, loops and boolean chains) and name it. Then answer Q1, Q2, Q3 and Q4 from the protocol as true or false, each with one sentence of evidence from the file, and write a one-line note of the form "methodName: what it does". Do NOT derive or state the category; the mapping is applied later.
4. Blindness: do not try to read anything outside the current directory and do not try to find out anything about these classes beyond the file itself.
5. Answer with one entry per id of the batch, all 20 of them, in the required JSON form.

evidence.q4: No switch; complexity is null/handle checks and the anonymous read/write bodies with map lookups and error branches.

readings.note: create: returns a nullSafe TypeAdapter that reads the type label to pick a delegate adapter and writes the label into the serialized object.

evidence.q1: updateItems is a layout pass that computes each tab's type, selects the current one, records currentTabs and then resizes tabs, i.e. it sets the bar's own state from the parsed tab list.
evidence.q2: All methods serve one widget: a bottom navigation bar with tabs, selection, shifting and background animations.
evidence.q3: It mostly manipulates its own child tabs and own fields (currentTabPosition, widths, colors); reads like tabView.isActive() are on its own children.
evidence.q4: No switch over a kind value; complexity is a loop with nested if/else on mode and index.

readings.note: updateItems: assigns type and selection state to each parsed BottomBarTab, wires click listeners, stores them and resizes them for the current mode.

evidence.q1: findEscapingField is a backward provenance analysis over expressions and reaching definitions that returns the field reference that escapes.
evidence.q2: All methods serve one rule: detect methods returning an internal array.
evidence.q3: It works on AST nodes, symbols and dataflow results, which are syntax-tree data, not behaviour-bearing objects to move logic into.
evidence.q4: The method is an instanceof chain over the single expression variable with short cases delegating to fromNamedReference/fromMethodCall etc.

readings.note: findEscapingField: recursively traces an expression (casts, conditionals, switches, array access, calls) back to an internal array field reference, if any.

evidence.q1: checkFactoryMethod validates by querying factoryMethod.hasNoParameter()/hasSingleParameterTyped and returnType.isAssignableTo, then throws; it computes no value or own state.
evidence.q2: All methods serve one concept: building a DataSetPropertyInfo from a getter and its annotation.
evidence.q3: Decisions are made on other behaviour-bearing objects' state (annotation.hasFactoryMethod(), factoryMethod.returnType().isAssignableTo(...)) and values are passed through from annotation getters.
evidence.q4: No switch; complexity is a boolean chain with a nested if.

readings.note: checkFactoryMethod: verifies the configured factory method exists with no or one int parameter and returns the item presentation model type, else throws.

evidence.q1: perform prompts the user and forwards to project.addNewMockService, mockService.addNewMockOperation, mockOperation.addNewMockResponse and SoapUI.getDesktop().showDesktopPanel, choosing the order of calls.
evidence.q2: The class is one UI action: add a request to a mock service.
evidence.q3: It uses chains like request.getOperation().getInterface().getProject() and mockOperation.getMockService() and copies response content, attachments and headers from WsdlResponse into the new WsdlMockResponse.
evidence.q4: No switch; complexity is a while loop with nested prompts and null checks.

readings.note: perform: picks or creates a mock service and operation for the request, adds a mock response copied from the actual response, and optionally opens the editor.

evidence.q1: getBoundFields walks the class hierarchy with reflection and computes the FieldsData maps of bound fields, returning them.
evidence.q2: All methods serve one concept: creating reflective TypeAdapters for ordinary classes and records.
evidence.q3: It works on java.lang.reflect Field/Class metadata and its own BoundField/FieldsData holders; no behaviour belongs to other classes.
evidence.q4: No switch over a kind value; complexity is a while over superclasses containing a for over fields with record/access checks.

readings.note: getBoundFields: collects serializable and deserializable fields of a type and its superclasses into BoundFields, handling records, access filters and duplicate names.

evidence.q1: test computes and returns a boolean deciding whether a recipient should receive the level-up broadcast.
evidence.q2: The class is a single predicate for level-up broadcast recipients.
evidence.q3: It decides on other objects' fields via chains like mmoBroadcastingPlayer.getPlayer().getWorld(), mcMMO.p.getGeneralConfig().isLevelUpBroadcastsPartyMembersOnly() and mmoListeningPlayer.getParty().
evidence.q4: No switch; complexity is nested if guards on party, world, distance and visibility.

readings.note: test: returns whether the listener (player or console) should receive the broadcaster's level-up message based on party, world, distance and visibility config.
